info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package team is your org's shared space: documents edited together, files, seats, and agents as teammates.

get.summary: Returns every org's team spaces, one page at a time: the org, the space's id and name, who created it, how many people are in it and when it was created.
get.description:
Returns every org's team spaces, one page at a time: the org, the
space's id and name, who created it, how many people are in it and when it was
created.

Pages by keyset: pass `next` back as `cursor`, so a deep page costs what the
first one does. `q` matches name, slug, org and id; `org` narrows to one tenant;
`org` with `user` (an IAM user id) lists the spaces that person is in. Member
counts come from IAM per row, and a row IAM did not answer for carries no count
while `degraded` names the gap. SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit is rows per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Cursor continues a listing: pass back the previous page's `next`. Omit it
for the first page.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Q is a case-insensitive substring match over the space's name, slug, org and
id.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort is `name`, `org` or `created`, with `:desc` for descending. Defaults to
`name`.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org narrows the directory to one tenant.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description:
User narrows it to the spaces one person is in: their IAM user id. Requires
Org, the tenant that person belongs to.

get.summary: Returns one space with everyone who holds a role in it: their account id, the name IAM holds for them, and the role — owners first, then admins, members and guests.
get.description:
Returns one space with everyone who holds a role in it: their account
id, the name IAM holds for them, and the role — owners first, then admins,
members and guests. A space the org does not own is 404. SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the tenant that owns the space, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space id, from the path.

post.summary: Read the caller's account and switch space
post.description:
The account control plane the Team client speaks: one POST carries a `method` verb and its `params`, and answers {"result": …}. The verbs are the session's own reads and the space switch — getLoginInfoByToken, enrol, getUserWorkspaces, selectWorkspace, getWorkspaceInfo, getMemberships, getPerson, getSocialIds, getRegionInfo, isReadOnlyGuest — plus sendInvite, which adds a member to a space and is refused for a caller who is not its owner or admin.

A REFUSAL IS HTTP 200 carrying {"error": {severity, code, params}} — the platform Status the client translates — not a 4xx. An unreadable body, an unauthorized session and an unknown verb all arrive that way, so a caller that reads only the status code reads every failure here as a success.

NO CREDENTIAL IS EVER HANDLED HERE. login, signUp, the OTP verbs, password change and reset, join and the guest-token exchange each answer Unauthorized with "sign in at hanzo.id" — a stated policy, not an unknown method, so the refusal is a fact a test can pin. Sessions come from the OAuth pair under /account/auth.

Auth is the team session token: Authorization: Bearer, else the HttpOnly account-token cookie. The tenant is that token's SIGNED org claim, never a header, and selectWorkspace resolves only among the orgs the token proves membership of. It also demands an explicit workspaceUrl — it never falls back to a first space, and a slug that resolves in two of the caller's orgs answers Ambiguous rather than picking one.

get.summary: Start a sign-in at hanzo.id
get.description:
STARTS the OAuth hop: answers 302 to hanzo.id's authorize endpoint and sets the short-lived HttpOnly state cookie that binds the flow to this browser. NO TOKEN COMES BACK FROM THIS CALL — the session is minted by the callback below, and a client that expects JSON here gets a redirect with no body.

A browser is the intended caller. Anything else must follow the Location AND keep the Set-Cookie, because the callback refuses a flow whose state it cannot match. That cookie carries the random nonce plus the client's navigateUrl, so the round trip needs no second channel, and it lives ten minutes — the whole budget for the hop.

The provider segment only picks a hint: the redirect_uri is ALWAYS the canonical openid callback, the one IAM has registered. Measured end to end, hanzo.id strips that hint today, so /auth/google and /auth/openid land on the same Hanzo sign-in page — the federation shortcut is an upstream fix, not a second endpoint here.

get.summary: Complete a sign-in and hand the browser its session
get.description:
COMPLETES the OAuth hop: hanzo.id redirects the browser here with ?code and ?state, and the answer is another 302 — back to the client's login route carrying the freshly minted team session token in the query. Never JSON, and never a token in this response's own body.

THE STATE IS CHECKED FIRST, before the code is even looked at: the flow cookie is read and cleared one-shot, and a callback whose ?state does not equal the nonce it held is bounced with error=state_mismatch and NEVER exchanged. That is what makes a forged or replayed callback inert. Only then is the code exchanged server-side — team is a confidential client with a client_secret, so there is no PKCE and the code never passes through the browser's JS.

The tenant is derived from the IAM access token VERIFIED RS256 against the JWKS, the same trust anchor the identity boundary uses; a token whose owner claim is empty fails closed with no login at all. Every org that token proves gets a space ensured, so a member of two orgs is a counted seat in both. The IAM access token is also parked in an HttpOnly cookie for the same-origin agents proxy — page JS never reads it.

EVERY failure is a redirect, not a status: a denied consent, a missing code, a failed exchange, an unreadable userinfo, an unverifiable org and a token-mint failure each bounce to the login page with an ?error code naming the step.

delete.summary: Signs this browser out of team by expiring the HttpOnly account-token cookie the OAuth callback set.
delete.description:
Signs this browser out of team by expiring the HttpOnly
account-token cookie the OAuth callback set. It is the counterpart of the
cookie PUT, it takes nothing — the cookie it clears is named by this service,
never by the caller — and it is unconditional: a caller with no cookie, an
expired one or a forged one all get the same acknowledgement, because clearing
something that is not there is the same outcome as clearing something that is.

It clears ONLY the team session cookie. The IAM access-token cookie the same
callback set is a different credential with a different lifetime and is left
alone, so this is a team sign-out, not a platform one.

put.summary: Store the session token as this browser's cookie
put.description:
Writes the team session token into the HttpOnly `account-token` cookie — Secure, SameSite=Lax, whole-origin scope, thirty days — and answers {"result": true}. This is how the client turns the token it caught off the OAuth bounce into a credential page JS can no longer read, which IS the security property: script that cannot see the cookie cannot exfiltrate it, and every later call on the files, billing and collaborator planes authenticates from it when no bearer is sent.

The token is VERIFIED — signature and expiry, against this service's own signing secret — BEFORE it is stored. Anything this service did not sign is 401 and nothing is written; persisting a caller-supplied value unchecked would be a session-fixation hole, where an attacker pins a cookie the victim's browser then presents as its own.

The token may arrive as `token` in the JSON body or, when the body is absent or unparseable, from the Authorization bearer — an unreadable body is NOT an error here. The sibling DELETE clears this same cookie and signs the browser out of team only: the IAM cookie set alongside it is a different credential with its own lifetime and is left alone.

get.summary: Returns the identity providers this deployment starts a login with.
get.description:
Returns the identity providers this deployment starts a login
with. It is always exactly one — hanzo.id. Which identities that provider accepts
(Google, GitHub, passkey, password) is IAM's question, answered on IAM's own
page next to the identity check and the training-data consent that must
precede a first session; listing them here would be a second place holding
that answer, and the two drift the moment IAM gains or drops one.

get.summary: Returns the plan and seat counts for the caller's OWN org, resolved from the VERIFIED team session token — never a client header.
get.description:
Returns the plan and seat counts for the caller's OWN org, resolved
from the VERIFIED team session token — never a client header. Seats and guests
are the org's distinct active human members (a bot member is not a seat); the
plan comes from the licensing entitlement and is empty when that read is
unavailable, so the page shows an honest dash rather than a fabricated tier. A
caller with no verified session gets 401, and a real seat-read failure is a
502 rather than a false "0 members".

get.summary: Open the wallet page
get.description:
Serves the usage-and-wallet page the Team front links to — HTML, not JSON. It is a static React build compiled into this binary, so there is no upstream to be down and no build step at request time.

SESSION-GATED: without a verified team session token — bearer, else the HttpOnly account cookie — the caller gets 401 and not one byte of the page, so an anonymous browser meets a refusal rather than a shell that then fails to load anything.

The page is markup only. It reads money SAME-ORIGIN from cloud's own balance and usage endpoints, which pin the org from the IAM cookie the team OAuth callback set — nothing under this path proxies a money read, so there is no second auth mechanism here to get wrong. A deployment whose page was never built answers 503 naming the missing bundle, never a blank 200.

get.summary: Load an asset of the wallet page
get.description:
Serves one file of the embedded wallet bundle — a content-hashed script or stylesheet under assets/, an icon, or the page shell itself.

A path that names NO REAL FILE falls back to the shell instead of 404ing, which is what makes a deep link into the page's own routes survive a hard refresh. So a 200 here is not proof the asset exists — a typo answers HTML.

assets/ is immutable for a year (the names carry the content hash); the shell is no-cache, so a deploy is picked up on the next load. Gated exactly like the page: 401 without a verified session, 503 when the bundle was never built.

get.summary: Returns the channels the caller may see, with the kind and work facet each carries.
get.description:
Returns the channels the caller may see, with the kind and work
facet each carries.

A signed-in TEAM MEMBER reads every channel of every space they are in that is
open to them: public channels, and the private channels and direct messages
that name them. An APPLICATION of the org (its own machine credential) reads
the public channels of the org's spaces and nothing that belongs to
particular people. Anybody else without a team session is 401.

It reads the SAME Chunter documents the transactor serves, so a channel opened
in the Team client appears here with no sync, and a facet written here is read
by anything holding the document.

post.summary: Opens a named channel and answers it as the store now holds it.
post.description:
Opens a named channel and answers it as the store now holds it.

It writes through the SAME applyTx path the Team client uses, so a channel opened
here is broadcast to every live client of the space and appears in an open
sidebar without a reload — the same property listChannels rests on, read from the
write side.

A SIGNED-IN TEAM MEMBER opens it as themselves: they are its first member and
its owner, every other member named must be somebody the space knows (a person
in it, or one of the org's agents), and a guest may not open channels at all. An
application of the org opens it as the org, with exactly the members it names.
Anybody else without a team session is 401.

TWO TRANSACTIONS, NOT ONE, when the request states a facet. The document and
its mixin are separate writes in this model (bindChannel writes only the second),
and composing them here rather than inventing a combined tx keeps one write
path for each. A create that lands and a facet that does not is visible as a
channel with default intent, which is the honest partial state.

patch.summary: Renames a channel, sets its topic, or archives or reopens it, and answers the channel as it now stands.
patch.description:
Renames a channel, sets its topic, or archives or reopens it, and
answers the channel as it now stands.

Its owners and the space's admins may edit a channel; a channel nobody owns — one
opened by an integration — may be edited by anyone in it, and a direct
message by either person in it. Archiving withdraws a public channel from the
cross-org directory in the same write; reopening lists it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel, from the path.

put.summary: States what a channel is for: its lifecycle intent, and what it is about.
put.description:
States what a channel is for: its lifecycle intent, and what it is
about. It answers the channel as it now stands.

The write is a platform MIXIN on the channel document, applied through the
SAME applyTx path the Team client's own writes take and broadcast to every
connected client — so a channel bound here updates live in an open space
rather than on the next reload. A team member binds a channel they can see; an
application of the org binds its public channels only; anybody else without
a team session is 401.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the channel to bind, from the path. The URL is the authority; a body
carrying another id cannot redirect the write.

get.summary: Returns the people and agents in one channel, as the roster describes them.
get.description:
Returns the people and agents in one channel, as the roster
describes them. The caller must be able to see the channel.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel, from the path. The URL is the authority.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description:
Space names the space holding the channel, and is required for the reason the
bind op requires it: a channel id is unique within a space and not across the
org, so searching every space for a match would make the answer depend on
iteration order.

post.summary: Adds people to a channel and answers the channel as it now stands.
post.description:
Adds people to a channel and answers the channel as it now stands.

Anyone in the space except a guest may join a public channel by naming
themselves. Adding somebody else takes being in the channel already (or
administering the space, for a channel they can see). A direct message's people
are what it is, so none can be added — open another one. Everyone added must
be a member of the space or one of the org's agents; an agent added to a channel
answers when it is @-mentioned there.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel, from the path.

delete.summary: Takes one person out of a channel — the caller leaving, when the account is their own.
delete.description:
Takes one person out of a channel — the caller leaving, when the
account is their own. Removing somebody else takes owning the channel or
administering the space. Leaving a channel you are not in, or removing somebody
who is not there, changes nothing. A direct message cannot be left: its people
are what it is. Answers 204.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel, from the path.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account is the account uuid to remove, from the path. Your own is leaving.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid holding the channel.

get.summary: Returns the tail of one channel's conversation, oldest first, each message with its reactions, files and thread count.
get.description:
Returns the tail of one channel's conversation, oldest first, each
message with its reactions, files and thread count.

It reads the SAME Chunter documents the transactor serves, so a message typed
in the Team client is here with no sync. A team member reads any channel they
may see; an application of the org reads public channels only; anybody else
without a team session is 401. A channel the caller may not read answers 404
rather than 403, so a probe learns nothing about what exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel, from the path. The URL is the authority.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description:
Space names the space holding the channel, and is required for the reason the
bind op requires it: a channel id is unique within a space and not across the
org, so searching every space for a match would make the answer depend on
iteration order.

post.summary: Says one thing in a channel, as the caller.
post.description:
Says one thing in a channel, as the caller.

The write goes through the SAME applyTx path the Team client's own messages
take and is broadcast to every connected client of the space, so a message
sent here appears live in an open channel rather than on the next reload. It
answers the message as the store now HOLDS it.

`<@account-uuid>` in the text is stored as the platform's mention, so the
person is notified in their inbox. Mentioning one of the org's agents — or
writing in a direct message with one — wakes it: it runs as itself, on behalf
of the caller, and posts its answer into the same channel. The caller must be
able to see the channel, and an archived channel refuses new messages (409).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the channel to say it in, from the path.

example.text: deploying now, <@9f2c…> can you watch the dashboards?

get.summary: Open the live collaborative-editing socket
get.description:
Upgrades to the hocuspocus WebSocket the Team editor syncs its Y.js documents over: binary frames of document name, message type and payload, with ONE socket multiplexing every document a tab has open. The server is a relay and an ordered update log, not a CRDT engine — it replays the log to each joining peer and broadcasts every update to the rest, which converges because Y.js updates are commutative and idempotent. There is no body; the response is a protocol upgrade.

BOTH LANES SHARE ONE ROOT. The client derives them from one configured URL — this socket at its root, the markup-snapshot RPC one segment in — so pointing the editor at this service is one value, and the two lanes cannot drift apart.

AUTH IS IN-BAND, PER DOCUMENT, NOT ON THE UPGRADE. The handshake gates only on browser Origin (403 outside the team surfaces; no Origin at all is admitted, which is what a non-browser sends), and then the first frame for a document must be an Auth message carrying the same session or space token every other team route verifies — a browser WebSocket cannot set an Authorization header, which is why the token rides inside the protocol. Anything else on an unauthenticated document is answered with one permission denial and nothing further.

Every document is authorized on its own: the document's space must be the token's space when the token pins one, and the caller must be a member of it. A mismatch, an unknown space and a non-member deny alike with "document not found". Rooms are keyed by org and space and the persisted log's key embeds both, so a foreign document id can neither join a room nor read a blob.

The server pings every twenty seconds and drops a socket silent for sixty, so a backgrounded tab — whose JS timers are throttled but whose network stack still auto-pongs — stays connected instead of dying into a reconnect loop.

post.summary: CollabRPC is the collaborative-markup snapshot plane the Team front's editor speaks: createContent stores a document field's markup at a fresh, immutable blob ref and returns it, updateContent stores a new snapshot and answers nothing, and getContent reads back the exact snapshot a ref names.
post.description:
CollabRPC is the collaborative-markup snapshot plane the Team front's editor
speaks: createContent stores a document field's markup at a fresh, immutable
blob ref and returns it, updateContent stores a new snapshot and answers
nothing, and getContent reads back the exact snapshot a ref names.

createContent ALSO seeds the live-editing update log from the front-supplied
Y.js update, so a dialog-authored description is visible in the collaborative
editor — which replays that log — and not only in snapshot reads.
updateContent never touches that log: peers may be live-editing the document,
and their edits are not this call's to overwrite.

Every call is scoped to the caller's VERIFIED session or space token: the
documentId's space must be the token's space when the token names one,
and the caller must be a member of it. An unknown space, another tenant's
space and a space the caller is not in all answer the same 404, so a
probe learns nothing about what exists.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description:
DocumentID addresses the document field, as
"<spaceUuid>|<objectClass>|<objectId>|<objectAttr>" — the
collaborator-client encodeDocumentId shape, from the path.

post.summary: Opens the direct message between the caller and the people named, or answers the one that already exists — there is one conversation per set of people, however many times it is asked for.
post.description:
Opens the direct message between the caller and the people named,
or answers the one that already exists — there is one conversation per set of
people, however many times it is asked for.

Every person named must be a member of the space or one of the org's agents;
a direct message with an agent is a conversation it answers every message in,
and a guest may not open one.
Answers 201 when this call opened it and 200 when it was already there.

get.summary: Returns the documents of a space the caller may see, with the teamspaces they are grouped in.
get.description:
Returns the documents of a space the caller may see, with the
teamspaces they are grouped in.

These are the Team client's own document rows, so a page created there is
here with no sync. Each carries the `collaborator` id its body opens with on
the /v1/team/collaborator socket. A private teamspace's documents are listed
only for its members.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

parameters.name: teamspace
parameters.description: Teamspace narrows the answer to one teamspace.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Parent narrows the answer to one document's children.

post.summary: Creates a document, as the caller, after its siblings.
post.description:
Creates a document, as the caller, after its siblings.

It is created through the Team client's own write path, so it appears in an
open Documents sidebar live, and its author is subscribed to it: a comment on
it lands in their inbox. Its body starts empty — open the returned
`collaborator` id on the /v1/team/collaborator socket to write it.

A space whose caller can write no teamspace at all gets one on its first
document: a public "General" teamspace every current member of the space is
in, which is what the Team client would otherwise make somebody create by hand
before the first page. Guests and agents are not made members of it.

delete.summary: Removes a document with everything nested under it and every comment on any of them — the Team client's own delete, which takes the subtree with it.
delete.description:
Removes a document with everything nested under it and every
comment on any of them — the Team client's own delete, which takes the
subtree with it. Its author, an owner of its teamspace or an admin of the
space may delete it. Answers 204.

The document model has no archived state for a page (only a teamspace can be
archived), so there is nothing softer to offer here than removal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the document, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid holding it.

get.summary: Returns one document the caller may see.
get.description: Returns one document the caller may see.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the document, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid holding it.

patch.summary: Renames a document or moves it — under another document, to the top of its teamspace, or to another teamspace with everything nested under it.
patch.description:
Renames a document or moves it — under another document, to the top
of its teamspace, or to another teamspace with everything nested under it.

Anyone who can write the teamspace may rename or move a page, as in the Team
client. A move goes after its new siblings, and a document cannot be moved
under itself or under one of its own descendants.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the document, from the path.

get.summary: Returns the comments on a document, oldest first — the same message shape a channel's conversation answers.
get.description:
Returns the comments on a document, oldest first — the same
message shape a channel's conversation answers.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the document, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid holding it.

post.summary: Comments on a document, as the caller.
post.description:
Comments on a document, as the caller.

It is a message attached to the document, written through the Team client's
own path: the people subscribed to the document and anyone mentioned are
notified, and an agent mentioned answers with a comment of its own. It can be
replied to, reacted to, edited and deleted with the message ops.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the document, from the path.

get.summary: Stream live changes to what the caller may see, as Server-Sent Events

post.summary: Upload a file into a space
post.description:
Stores one file in a space's blob store and answers the blob id it is addressable by, as plain text — the front discards that body, it is there for a caller driving this by hand.

The body is a multipart form with a `file` part, and THAT PART'S FILENAME IS THE BLOB ID: the client mints it (a uuid v4) and the server stores under it, so a part whose filename is not a uuid is refused rather than assigned one. A file over 100 MiB is 413 and an empty one is 400.

The caller must hold a verified session or space token AND be a member of the space; an unknown space, another tenant's space and a space the caller is not in all answer the same 404, so a probe learns nothing about what exists. The stored key embeds the verified org and the space, so an upload cannot land in another tenant's box whatever id it names. A storage backend that is unavailable fails closed with 502 rather than reporting a write it never made.

delete.summary: Removes one blob from a space's file store.
delete.description:
Removes one blob from a space's file store. The caller must
hold a verified session AND be a member of the space; anything else — an
unknown space, another tenant's space, a space the caller is not
in — answers the same 404, so a probe learns nothing about what exists.

It is IDEMPOTENT: deleting a present or an absent blob both answer 204, so a
delete never confirms a blob's existence and a foreign blob id (a physical key
the caller can never name into another tenant's box) is a harmless no-op. A
storage backend that is unavailable fails closed with 502 rather than lying
about success.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid the blob belongs to, from the path.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description:
Filename is the last path segment, which the front sets to the blob id
when it sends no explicit `file`.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: File is the blob id, and wins over the path segment when both are present.

get.summary: Download a space file
get.description:
Streams one blob's raw BYTES back — this is the read side of the space file store, not a JSON envelope around it.

THE BLOB IS NAMED BY THE `file` QUERY PARAMETER, NOT BY :filename. The path segment is only the name a browser saves the download under; a request without ?file= is a 400 no matter what the path says.

The Content-Type is derived from the STORED BYTES, never from the name: only png, jpeg, gif and webp, recognized by their magic bytes, are served inline under their true type, and everything else is served inert as application/octet-stream with an attachment disposition. Every response carries nosniff, so a file uploaded under an .svg or .html name cannot be talked into executing in a viewer's origin. Blobs are immutable, so a hit caches privately for a year.

Same gate as the upload: verified token, membership of the space. A genuine miss, another tenant's space, a space the caller is not in, and a blob id belonging to a different space are ONE answer — 404 — because the physical key is org- and space-scoped and a foreign id is simply a key that does not exist. An unavailable backend is a 502, never an empty 200.

get.summary: Returns the caller's notifications, newest first, each with the channel or document it is about and the message that caused it.
get.description:
Returns the caller's notifications, newest first, each with the
channel or document it is about and the message that caused it.

These are the rows the Team client's Inbox reads, so a notification cleared
there is cleared here. Only the caller's own notifications are ever listed.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Archived lists the archived notifications instead of the live ones.

post.summary: Marks every live notification of the caller's read, and says how many it changed.
post.description:
Marks every live notification of the caller's read, and
says how many it changed.

post.summary: Archives one of the caller's notifications — read, and out of the live inbox — and answers it.
post.description:
Archives one of the caller's notifications — read, and
out of the live inbox — and answers it. It is listed again with
`archived=true`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the notification, from the path.

post.summary: Marks one of the caller's notifications read and answers it.
post.description:
Marks one of the caller's notifications read and answers it.
Another person's notification is a 404, as one that does not exist is.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the notification, from the path.

get.summary: Returns the people and agents in a space, with the name, avatar, role and presence a client draws them with.
get.description:
Returns the people and agents in a space, with the name, avatar,
role and presence a client draws them with.

People come from IAM, the membership authority; agents from the org's agent
registry; avatars from the Person documents the Team client edits. An IAM that
does not answer is a 502 rather than an empty roster, and an agent registry
that does not answer is named in `degraded` beside the people who did load.
The caller must be a member of the space.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

delete.summary: Removes a message, with its replies, reactions, files and the inbox notifications that point at it.
delete.description:
Removes a message, with its replies, reactions, files and the
inbox notifications that point at it. Its author may delete it, and so may an
owner or admin of the space.

Each removal is a platform remove through the Team client's write path, so the
message disappears from every open client live. Answers 204.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description:
Space names the space holding it. A message id is unique within a space,
not across the org.

patch.description:
Rewrites what a message says. Only its author may edit it.

The edit is an ordinary update of the message document through the Team
client's own write path, stamped with editedOn, so an open client shows the
new text and the "edited" mark live. Somebody the new text mentions for the
first time is notified.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message, from the path.

delete.summary: Takes back the caller's reaction to a message and answers the message with its reactions as they now stand.
delete.description:
Takes back the caller's reaction to a message and answers the message
with its reactions as they now stand. Taking back a reaction the caller never
made changes nothing and is not an error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message, from the path.

parameters.name: emoji
parameters.description: Emoji is the reaction, from the path (percent-encoded on the wire).

parameters.name: space
parameters.description: Space names the space holding the message.

put.summary: Adds the caller's reaction to a message and answers the message with its reactions as they now stand.
put.description:
Adds the caller's reaction to a message and answers the message with
its reactions as they now stand. Reacting twice with one emoji is one
reaction: the second call changes nothing.

The emoji is the last path segment, percent-encoded — PUT
/v1/team/messages/7a1c/reactions/%F0%9F%91%8D for 👍.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message, from the path.

parameters.name: emoji
parameters.description: Emoji is the reaction, from the path (percent-encoded on the wire).

get.summary: Returns a message's thread, oldest first, each reply with its reactions and files.
get.description:
Returns a message's thread, oldest first, each reply with its
reactions and files.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message, from the path.

parameters.name: space
parameters.description:
Space names the space holding it. A message id is unique within a space,
not across the org.

post.summary: Answers a message in its thread, as the caller.
post.description:
Answers a message in its thread, as the caller.

A reply is a thread message attached to the one it answers, written through
the Team client's own path: the parent's reply count and last-reply time move
with it, the people already in the thread and anyone mentioned are notified,
and an agent mentioned in a reply answers in the same thread. A reply cannot
itself be replied to — threads are one level deep, as in the Team client.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the message being answered, from the path.

get.summary: Lists the channels orgs have published, across every org.
get.description:
Lists the channels orgs have published, across every org.

It is NOT part of GET /channels, and the separation is the point: that address
answers the CALLER'S channels, so folding these in would put strangers' channels
in somebody's own sidebar.

It reads the directory and never a tenant's store. Every field it can answer
with is one an org published by making a channel public, so there is nothing here
to scope by org — a directory only its own org can read is not a directory.
An authenticated principal is still required, because an anonymous crawler is
not who this is for.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Q matches a channel's name or its topic.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org narrows to one org's published channels.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps the page, 50 when unstated and 200 at most. An unparseable
value reads as unstated rather than as zero — zero pages is not an answer
anybody asked for.

get.summary: Returns the transactor's live sessions for the space the caller's credential names — the endpoint the front's space switcher and server panel poll on the transactor base.
get.description:
Returns the transactor's live sessions for the space the caller's
credential names — the endpoint the front's space switcher and server panel
poll on the transactor base. `token` carries the same two lanes the socket's path
segment does: a space UUID names the space and is authorized against the
membership rows, an HS256 space token names it in its signed claims.
activeSessions carries ONLY that one space, never another tenant's sessions.
An unverifiable credential, or one the caller is no member under, is 401.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Token is the space token minted by selectWorkspace.

get.summary: Open the space data-plane socket
get.description:
Upgrades to the WebSocket the Team client runs an entire space over: every frame is a ZAP envelope wrapping one JSON-RPC message — findAll/findOne reads against the space's documents, tx writes that broadcast to the other live sessions, hello negotiating JSON rather than msgpack. The response is a protocol upgrade, so there is no body to read.

THE PATH SEGMENT IS THE CREDENTIAL. It is the space token selectWorkspace minted — bearer-equivalent, and sitting in a URL that proxies and access logs record, which is exactly why it expires in twelve hours and is re-minted on demand rather than being long-lived like the session token. It is decoded and verified (signature and expiry) BEFORE the upgrade, so a bad one is a 401 and never a socket that is accepted and then dropped, and it must carry both an account and a space claim. Nothing ambient authorizes this socket: a WebSocket is exempt from CORS, so a cookie-borne credential would make the Origin check the only access control on the whole data plane.

The tenant is the token's SIGNED org claim and it keys every store path, so no header can name another space's data. The upgrade ALSO refuses a browser Origin outside the team surfaces with 403 — otherwise any page could open an authenticated socket with a token it lured out of a logged-in browser — while a request with no Origin at all is admitted, because that is what a non-browser client sends.

On connect the space's system spaces are seeded once and the roster is reconciled every time, so the org's human members and its bots are present as space people without a separate sync call.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

displayName.description:
DisplayName is the human label for the sign-in button; this deployment
sends "Hanzo". Omitted from the body when empty.

name.description:
Name is the provider id, and it is the value that goes back in the URL to
start a login: GET /v1/team/account/auth/{provider}. This deployment
surfaces exactly one, "openid" — the hanzo.id provider.

content.description: Content maps a document field to its ProseMirror markup JSON.

source.description:
Source is the blob ref a getContent reads the snapshot from. Absent means
there is no snapshot to read, which answers empty content.

updates.description:
Updates carries, per field, a base64 Y.js state update encoding the SAME
markup — the front computes it (markupToYDoc → encodeStateAsUpdate) so a
createContent seeds the live-editing lane's update log, not just the
snapshot blob. Without it a dialog-created description is invisible in the
collaborative editor, which replays the ydoc log, never the snapshot.

documentId.description:
DocumentID addresses the document field, as
"<spaceUuid>|<objectClass>|<objectId>|<objectAttr>" — the
collaborator-client encodeDocumentId shape, from the path.

method.description: Method is the verb: createContent, updateContent or getContent.

content.description:
Content maps each document field to its value for the verb: the new blob
ref after a createContent, the stored markup after a getContent.

error.description:
Error carries a SEMANTIC refusal, which this RPC reports under 200 because
the client throws on result.error — auth and tenancy failures are HTTP
statuses instead.

result.description: Result is true when the cookie was written or cleared.

channel.description: Channel addresses it in the owning store — what a join is called with.

members.description: Members counts the channel, and never names anybody in it.

name.description: Name is what a person sees, without the sigil a client draws.

org.description: Org owns the channel. It is also what a caller filters by to browse one org.

space.description: Space is where the channel lives inside that org.

topic.description: Topic is the channel's one-line subject, empty when it has none.

updated.description: Updated is when this row was last written, unix seconds.

active.description: Active is whether that plan's entitlement is live.

guestLimit.description: GuestLimit is the plan's team.guests cap, when the plan carries one.

guests.description: Guests is how many of those seats are guests.

plan.description:
Plan is the licensed plan id, empty when it cannot be resolved here — an
honest dash on the page, never a fabricated tier.

seats.description: Seats is the org's distinct active human members.

upgradeUrl.description: UpgradeURL is where the page sends a caller who wants a bigger plan.

channels.description: Channels is every published channel the query matched, newest-written first.

admin.description: Admin is the upstream service's server-panel flag, always false here.

metrics.description:
Metrics is the upstream transactor's metrics block. This server does not
populate it, so it is always the empty object — the front reads the key,
not its contents.

activeSessions.description:
ActiveSessions maps a space uuid to its connected sessions. It carries
only the token's OWN space, and is empty for a token that names none.

userId.description: UserID is the account the session is authenticated as.

archived.description:
Archived reports that the channel has been closed. It is the platform's own
Space attribute — the same one the Team client writes — and NOT a field of
the work facet, so there is exactly one answer to "is this channel open".

bindings.description:
Bindings are what this channel is ABOUT, each a "<kind>:<ref>" string —
"project:acme/web", "repo:hanzoai/cloud", "issue:1010". One list rather
than one field per kind, because the next thing a channel can be about should
not be a schema change; and a bound value is opaque here on purpose, since
the app that owns a project is the app that can resolve one. HIP-0523 §2:
a binding is a REFERENCE, never a copy — a channel holding an issue's title or
status would be the parallel work-item store HIP-1160 §1 forbids.

direct.description:
Direct reports that this is a channel between people rather than a named
channel. It is derived from the document's class, so it cannot disagree
with what the client will render.

id.description:
ID is the channel document's own id, and the value the bind op addresses.
It is unique within a space, not across the org.

kind.description:
Kind is what sort of channel this is: "public" (open to everyone in the
space), "private" (open to its members) or "dm" (a conversation between
the people in it). It is derived from the class and the private flag, so it
cannot disagree with Direct and Private beside it.

life.description:
Life is the channel's lifecycle INTENT — "standing" or "bound" (HIP-0523 §2).
Absent on the document it reads "standing": a channel nobody classified is one
that persists.

members.description:
Members are the account uuids in the channel, agents included: an agent
projects as a space member under a uuid derived from its id, so a
caller comparing this against GET /v1/bot/members learns which channels an
agent is in.

name.description:
Name is what a person sees in a sidebar. A direct message carries none, so
this is empty for one — the members are its name.

private.description: Private reports that the channel is restricted to its members.

space.description:
Space is the space uuid holding this channel. It is part of the
channel's address: two spaces of one org may each hold a channel with
the same name, and only the pair identifies one.

topic.description: Topic is the channel's own one-line subject, as the Team client sets it.

bindings.description:
Bindings REPLACES what the channel is about, wholly. It is a replace and
not a merge because a caller that cannot remove a binding would have no way
to correct a wrong one, and an empty list sent explicitly is how a channel
is unbound. Absent (null) leaves the existing list alone.

id.description:
ID is the channel to bind, from the path. The URL is the authority; a body
carrying another id cannot redirect the write.

life.description:
Life sets the lifecycle intent: "standing" or "bound". Any other
value is refused rather than stored, so a reader never has to interpret a
third one. Empty leaves the current intent unchanged.

space.description:
Space names the space holding the channel. It is required, because
a channel id is unique only within one and searching every space for a
matching id would make the write's target depend on iteration order.

archived.description:
Archived closes the channel (true) or reopens it (false). An archived channel
keeps its history and takes no new messages.

id.description: ID is the channel, from the path.

name.description: Name renames a channel. A direct message has no name.

space.description: Space is the space uuid holding it. Body-only.

topic.description: Topic sets the channel's one-line subject; "" clears it.

id.description: ID is the channel, from the path.

members.description:
Members are the account uuids to add — people or agents of the space.
Naming only yourself joins a public channel.

space.description: Space is the space uuid holding it. Body-only.

members.description:
Members are the channel's people and agents, as the roster describes them.
An account the space no longer knows is listed by id, with no role.

bindings.description: Bindings are what the channel is about, each "<kind>:<ref>".

life.description: Life is the lifecycle intent, "standing" or "bound"; empty reads standing.

members.description:
Members are the account uuids in the channel. A public channel may open empty —
anyone in the org can find it — and a private one that names nobody is
refused rather than created unreachable.

name.description:
Name is what a person sees in a sidebar — "bugfix-1010", not "#bugfix-1010".
The sigil is how a client DRAWS a channel, and storing it would put it in the
name twice the first time a client added its own.

private.description:
Private restricts the channel to its members. Public is the default because a
channel nobody can find is the more surprising of the two.

space.description:
Space is where the channel is opened. Optional: an org with one space has no
choice to make, so it does not have to state one. An org with several must,
because picking for it would make the channel's home depend on iteration order.

topic.description: Topic is the channel's one-line subject.

channel.description: Channel is the channel as it now stands, in the listing's shape.

channels.description:
Channels is every channel of every space the caller's org owns, each
with the work facet it carries.

files.description: Files attaches blobs already uploaded to the space.

id.description: ID is the document, from the path.

space.description: Space is the space uuid holding it. Body-only.

text.description:
Text is the comment, with the same `<@account-uuid>` mentions a message
takes.

roster.description: Roster is everyone who holds a role in the space, owners first.

team.description: Team is the space, as the directory lists it.

channel.description: Channel is the direct message, as the channel listing answers it.

created.description:
Created is true when this call opened the conversation (201) and false
when it already existed (200).

members.description:
Members are the account uuids to talk to — people or agents of the space.
The caller is always in the conversation and need not name themselves; an
empty list is the caller's own notes-to-self conversation.

space.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

author.description: Author is the account uuid that created it.

collaborator.description:
Collaborator is the documentId to open the body with on the
/v1/team/collaborator Y.js socket:
"<space>|document:class:Document|<id>|content".

comments.description: Comments is how many comments it has.

createdOn.description: CreatedOn is when it was created, unix milliseconds.

id.description: ID is the document's own id.

modifiedOn.description:
ModifiedOn is when its title or place last changed, unix milliseconds.
Edits to the body happen on the collaborator socket and do not move it.

parent.description:
Parent is the document this one is nested under. Empty for a document at
the top of its teamspace.

rank.description: Rank orders siblings: compare as plain strings, ascending.

space.description: Space is the space uuid holding it.

teamspace.description: Teamspace is the teamspace it belongs to.

id.description: ID is the document, from the path.

parent.description:
Parent moves the document under another one; "" moves it to the top of
its teamspace. It goes after its new siblings.

space.description: Space is the space uuid holding it. Body-only.

teamspace.description:
Teamspace moves the document — with everything nested under it — to
another teamspace, at the top unless Parent names a document there.

title.description: Title renames the document. Empty reads "Untitled".

parent.description: Parent nests the new document under another one.

space.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

teamspace.description:
Teamspace is where the document goes. Optional: a document nested under a
parent goes in the parent's teamspace, and a space with exactly one
teamspace the caller can write needs no name — with none, the first
document opens a public "General" teamspace for the whole space.

title.description:
Title is the document's title. Empty reads "Untitled", as in the Team
client.

docs.description:
Docs are the documents, grouped by teamspace, then parent, then the
order the Team client shows siblings in.

teamspaces.description:
Teamspaces are the teamspaces the caller may see, by name — the groups a
client draws the tree under.

file.description: File is the blob id, readable at GET /v1/team/files/{space}/{name}?file={file}.

id.description: ID is the attachment document's own id.

name.description: Name is the file's name as the person uploaded it.

size.description: Size is the file's length in bytes, as the uploader stated it.

type.description:
Type is the media type the uploader declared. The download route serves
what the BYTES are, not this; it is a hint for drawing an icon.

file.description:
File is the blob id — the uuid the file was uploaded under with
POST /v1/team/files/{space}. A blob of another space cannot be named: the
download is keyed by this message's space, so a foreign id resolves to
nothing.

name.description: Name is the file's name as a person should see it.

size.description: Size is the file's length in bytes.

type.description: Type is the file's media type, e.g. "image/png".

items.description: Items are the notifications, newest first, at most 200.

unread.description:
Unread is how many of the caller's live (unarchived) notifications are
unread — the number a badge shows, counted over all of them rather than
the page.

space.description: Space is the space uuid. Optional for a caller in exactly one space.

id.description: ID is the notification, from the path.

space.description: Space is the space uuid it was filed in. Body-only.

read.description: Read is how many notifications this call marked read.

archived.description: Archived reports that the caller archived it.

channel.description: Channel is the channel it is about, when it is about a channel.

createdOn.description: CreatedOn is when it was filed, unix milliseconds.

doc.description: Doc is the document it is about, when it is about a document.

id.description: ID is the notification's own id — what read and archive address.

message.description:
Message is the message that caused it, as the message ops answer it.
Absent when that message has since been deleted, or is in a channel the
caller can no longer see.

read.description: Read reports that the caller has seen it.

reason.description:
Reason is why it was filed: "mention", "dm" (a direct message), "reply" (in
a thread the caller is in), "comment" (on something the caller follows),
"assigned", or "other".

space.description: Space is the space uuid it was filed in.

thread.description: Thread is the message whose thread it is about, for a reply.

active.description:
Active is false for an agent the org has retired: it stays in the roster so
its past messages keep an author, and it no longer answers.

avatar.description:
Avatar is the blob id of an uploaded picture, readable at
GET /v1/team/files/{space}/avatar?file={avatar}. Empty when the person has
none and the client draws initials.

bot.description:
Bot reports that this member is one of the org's agents rather than a
person. An agent answers when it is @-mentioned or messaged directly.

id.description:
ID is the account uuid — the value every message's author, every channel's
members list and every `<@id>` mention token names.

name.description:
Name is what to call them: the name IAM holds for a person, the agent's
own name for an agent. Falls back to the id when neither has one.

personRef.description:
PersonRef is the member's Person document id, the reference a mention
stores.

presence.description:
Presence is "online" while the member holds a live connection to this
space (a Team client or an event stream), "offline" otherwise.

role.description:
Role is the member's role in the space — owner, admin, member or guest.
Agents read "member".

id.description: ID is the member's team account id.

name.description: Name is the name IAM holds for them.

role.description: Role is owner, admin, member or guest.

degraded.description:
Degraded names a roster source that did not answer — "agents" — so an
empty agent list reads as an outage rather than as an org with no agents.
Absent when every source answered.

members.description:
Members are the space's people and the org's agents, people first, each
group by name.

author.description:
Author is the team account uuid that wrote it. It is an ACCOUNT and not a
display name: what to call somebody is the roster's answer
(GET /v1/team/members), and copying it onto every message is how the two
come to disagree. An agent's messages carry the account derived from its
id, so the same field answers for both.

channel.description:
Channel is the channel it was said in — the same id the channel listing answers
with, so a caller holding a message can name its channel without a second read.
A reply names the channel its thread is in; a comment on a document has none.

createdOn.description: CreatedOn is unix MILLIseconds, which is what the platform stamps.

doc.description:
Doc is the document this message is a comment on. Empty for a message in a
channel.

editedOn.description:
EditedOn is when the author last edited the message, unix milliseconds.
Absent for a message never edited.

files.description: Files are the files attached to the message.

id.description: ID is the message document's own id.

lastReply.description:
LastReply is when the thread was last answered, unix milliseconds. Absent
for a message with no replies.

mentions.description:
Mentions are the account uuids the message @-mentions — exactly the
people notify.go told they were mentioned.

reactions.description:
Reactions are the emoji people reacted with, one entry per emoji, in the
order each emoji was first used.

replies.description: Replies is how many replies the message's thread holds.

text.description:
Text is the message as PLAIN TEXT. The document stores markup; this is the
same `plainText` reduction the agent responder reads a prompt with, so a
caller never has to parse the client's markup to know what was said. A
mention reads as "@Name" here and is listed by id in Mentions.

thread.description:
Thread is the message this one replies to. Empty for a message that starts
a conversation rather than answering one.

id.description: ID is the message, from the path.

space.description: Space names the space holding it. Body-only.

text.description:
Text is the message's new text, with the same `<@account-uuid>` mentions
a new message takes. Somebody newly mentioned is notified; somebody already
mentioned is not notified twice.

files.description:
Files attaches blobs already uploaded to the space. A message may be
files alone, with no text.

id.description: ID is the channel to say it in, from the path.

space.description:
Space names the space holding the channel. Body-only: a query string may not
redirect a write.

text.description:
Text is what to say, as plain text. It is wrapped in the client's markup on
the way in, so a caller writes words rather than HTML. `<@account-uuid>`
mentions a member of the space: it is stored as the platform's mention, so
they are notified, and an agent mentioned this way answers.

messages.description:
Messages are the conversation's, oldest first, at most `messageMax` of
them.

data.description: Data is the space and its roster. Null when the read failed.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

accounts.description: Accounts are the account uuids that reacted with it, earliest first.

count.description: Count is how many people reacted with it.

emoji.description: Emoji is the reaction itself, as the person picked it.
Emoji is the reaction, from the path (percent-encoded on the wire).

id.description: ID is the message, from the path.

space.description: Space names the space holding the message. Body-only.

files.description: Files attaches blobs already uploaded to the space.

id.description: ID is the message being answered, from the path.

space.description: Space names the space holding it. Body-only.

text.description:
Text is the reply, with the same `<@account-uuid>` mentions a message
takes.

created.description: Created is when the space was created (RFC 3339).

id.description:
ID is the space's stable id, the one every channel and document in it is filed
under.

members.description:
Members is how many people hold a role in the space. Absent when IAM did not
answer for this row, which `degraded` then names; never a zero standing in
for an unknown.

name.description: Name is the space's display name.

org.description: Org is the tenant that owns the space.

owner.description: Owner is the account that created the space.

ownerName.description:
OwnerName is the name IAM holds for that account, when they are still a
member.

slug.description: Slug is the space's URL handle, unique within its org.

archived.description:
Archived reports that the teamspace is closed: its documents still read,
and none can be created, moved into it, renamed or commented on.

id.description: ID is the teamspace document's id, the value teamDoc.teamspace names.

name.description: Name is what a person sees in a sidebar.

private.description: Private reports that the teamspace is open to its members only.

data.description: Data is one page of spaces. Null when the read failed.

degraded.description:
Degraded names a source that did not answer — "iam" — so a missing member
count reads as an outage rather than as an empty space.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

next.description: Next is the cursor for the following page, empty on the last one.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description:
Total counts every space matching the filters, across all pages. Absent when
the read failed.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
